hints.title: It is a directed graph
hints.body: Draw an edge from every cell to each neighboring cell with a larger value. The graph is acyclic because values strictly increase, and the answer is the longest path in this DAG.

hints.title: Memoize the search
hints.body: Let `best[r][c]` be the longest increasing path starting at cell `(r, c)`. It is one plus the best result among strictly larger neighbors.

hints.title: Process in elevation order
hints.body: Sort cells by elevation. When a cell is processed, every strictly smaller neighbor has already been processed, so its best value is final. Update from those smaller neighbors instead of using recursion.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
best = all ones
for each cell in increasing elevation order:
    for each neighbor with smaller elevation:
        best[cell] = max(best[cell], best[neighbor] + 1)
return maximum value in best
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete implementation.
